title: Machine-learning feature selection prioritizes CD101 in endometrial cancer expression data
summary: LASSO, SVM-RFE, random forest and XGBoost converged on CXCL12, LAYN and CD101 in an integrated endometrial-cancer transcriptomic study. The three-gene classifier separated tumor and nonmalignant tissues with reported AUCs 0.888, 0.837 and 0.848 across three public datasets. High CD101 expression was associated with poorer survival in an unadjusted 415-person TCGA subset. Single-cell discovery used only two tumors; the smallest bulk dataset contained seven cancers and five controls. Cell assays confirmed expression direction and successful CD101 mRNA knockdown, without demonstrating a downstream tumor function or clinical utility.

evidence.tested: Three-gene tissue discrimination in TCGA-UCEC, GSE17025 and GSE63678: AUC 0.888/0.837/0.848. The TCGA survival analysis used 415 cases and dataset-specific cutoffs without adjusted prognostic effects. qRT-PCR in Normal-EEC/Ishikawa cells reproduced expression direction; two siRNAs reduced CD101 mRNA.
evidence.unknown: Two-tumor single-cell discovery and small bulk comparisons limit generalization. Normal-only spatial references cannot establish tumor-specific localization. Protein localization, downstream function, causal immune regulation and clinical performance remain unestablished. Cell mRNA experiments do not convert the represented retrospective diagnostic/prognostic association into prospective validation.
evidence.ai_role: Four learned feature-selection approaches reduce eight intersecting transcriptomic candidates to a common three-gene set, which is assessed for tissue-class discrimination and exploratory outcome association.

source_review.scope: Full source-provenanced publisher HTML text independently read: study data/cohorts, learned-model Methods, relevant Results, experimental limits, affiliation and publication metadata. No underlying data reanalysis or supplementary-figure validation.
